_comment: Guided tours for the Trainer hub, one per overview page. Same contract as lessons/tour-content.json: beats highlight element ids via .tour-glow, audio per beat is optional (the tour falls back to a timer). Audio names: tour-<lang>-<page>-<n>.mp3 in trainer/audio/. The guide figure is never given a name. Built with scripts/site/build_trainer_tour.py.

index.idle: First time here? Get the 30-second overview.
index.done: That's the hub. Start with Present, and pick the session that fits your slot.

beats.text: Welcome to your trainer hub. Everything you need to run this training in your own market sits on this one page. Thirty seconds, and you will know where.
Present. Three ready sessions, from a fifteen-minute first look to a full sprint. One click opens a deck as your own copy in Google Slides, with the spoken script in the notes.
Learn it yourself. One deck per door of the platform, so you know exactly what your teams will see before you stand in front of them.
Plan your session. Your group answers a five-minute survey, and the planning Gem turns their answers into an agenda you shape. Planning becomes selection, not creation.
And when you are ready to roll out: four small moves in four weeks, written down, with the material for each move linked in place.

present.idle: New to the decks? Thirty seconds on how to pick one.
present.done: Pick by the slot you have, and hide what your group does not need.

beats.text: These are your three sessions. Pick by the slot you have, not by the topic; the content follows from your group's survey answers.
Fifteen minutes inside an existing team meeting is the safest first run, and it creates demand for the real session. One hour is your standard. Two hours adds sales-cycle steps.
Prefer to read? Every session also exists as a script page: each slide with its spoken text underneath, and your browser translates the whole thing in one right-click.

weeks.idle: Not sure where to start? Take the 30-second version.
weeks.done: Four small moves. Start by copying the survey.

beats.text: You do not need a launch event. You need four small moves in four weeks, each on material that already exists.
Before week one, copy the pre-survey and send your own copy, so the answers belong to you. Then book two slots: fifteen minutes in an existing meeting, and one hour for a real session.
Week one is the first look. Week two reads the survey and plans. Week three is the real session. And week four turns it into a routine, plus one short note back to the Academy.

selflearn.idle: Not sure which deck to read first? Thirty seconds.
selflearn.done: Read Start here first. The rest you can take door by door.

beats.text: These decks are not for presenting. They are for you, so you know exactly what your teams will see before you stand in front of them.

Start here explains the frame. Then one deck per door of the platform: quick help, the basics, the sales-cycle course, and the guide with its notebook. How you plan a session from these is its own deck, on the planning page.

plan.idle: First session to plan? Thirty seconds on the tools.
plan.done: Copy the survey first. Everything else follows from the answers.

beats.text: Planning a session here is selection, not creation. One deck explains the method in fifteen slides; then four tools do the sorting, and you stay the judge.
First the pre-survey. Copy it once, send your own copy, and the answers belong to you. Five minutes for each participant.

Then attach those answers to the planning Gem and name your session length. It drafts the blocks, the material, opening quotes from the group's own wishes, and what to skip. The notebook and the playbook answer every question about the materials.

faq.idle: Worried about the hard questions? Thirty seconds.
faq.done: Open the one you expect to hear. The answers are yours to use as they are.

beats.text: These are the objections you will actually hear, collected from the sales survey and the first trainings, roughly in the order they come up.
Every answer stands on the same two feet: the data rules are built into the lessons, and a person checks before anything reaches a customer. Say that early, not as a disclaimer at the end.

resistance.idle: Leadership says no time? Thirty seconds.
resistance.done: Make the ask small, and bring their own numbers.

beats.text: The most common blocker is not a skeptical seller. It is a sales leader whose calendar is full of revenue, and you are asking for a slice of it.
So make the ask small: fifteen minutes inside a meeting that already exists. There is no calendar cost, so there is nothing to refuse.
And argue with their own numbers. You have their team's survey answers; that turns an initiative from the Academy into what their people said last week.

quiet.idle: Usage fading after the start? Thirty seconds.
quiet.done: Small and regular beats big and rare.

beats.text: Every rollout dips after the first weeks. Expect it, and treat it as maintenance, not failure.
Usage survives on rhythm: the link stays in the meeting notes, one card of the week, and one question, what did you try and what did it save.
And when it has gone quiet, restart small. A fifteen-minute refresher with one card, or a colleague showing their own win. Never answer a dip with a bigger training.

progress.idle: What should you report? Thirty seconds.
progress.done: Three numbers, one win, one blocker. Ten minutes a month.

beats.text: Progress nobody sees does not exist, for your leadership or for the Academy. So keep the tracking light enough to survive a busy month.
Count three things: sessions and people, the content you ran, and the survey again after about eight weeks, so you can compare.
Then one short mail a month, always the same shape. The blocker line matters most; that is how the Academy learns where trainers need backup.

language.done: Translate the pages, and let the AI answer in your language.

beats.text: Everything here is written in English, but nobody has to wait for a translation. Your browser translates any page in one right-click, and it remembers your choice.

More importantly, the AI itself speaks your language. Write to Gemini and to the prepared Gems in your language and they answer in it, so coaching, negotiation practice and customer emails all happen locally.

One caveat worth saying in a session: the browser decides how it words a translated label, so a card can read slightly differently on your participants' screens than on your slide. Point at the position, and name the English original once.

playbook.idle: New to the playbook? Thirty seconds.
playbook.done: Read chapter one first. The rest is there when you need it.

beats.text: This is the short companion to the hub. It does not re-teach the AI content; the platform carries that, and the session decks carry the scripts.

Four short chapters: how to read a group and pick the content, the run sheet for a sprint day, two facilitation points, and the pre-session checklist. Chapter one is the one you will use before every session.
